stories.title: The Adventure of the Speckled Band

stories.end_marker: *** END OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK
stories.title: A Doll's House

probes.query: Remind me why the sisters locked their bedroom doors every night.
probes.rationale: Their stated reason is the roaming animals, not a known intruder.

any_of: I think that I mentioned to you that the Doctor kept a cheetah and a baboon. We had no feeling of security unless our doors were locked.

probes.query: What did Holmes learn about the money Roylott would lose if his stepdaughters married?
probes.rationale: Requires the current estate income and the marriage allowance, rather than merely a wedding mention.

any_of: not more than £ 750. Each daughter can claim an income of £ 250, in case of marriage.

probes.query: Keep the sleeping arrangement consistent: why was the furniture deliberately immobilized?
probes.rationale: The fixed bed keeps its occupant aligned with the delivery route. Two alternative explanations are accepted.

any_of: The lady could not move her bed. It must always be in the same relative position to the ventilator and to the rope
the bed was clamped to the floor, instantly gave rise to the suspicion that the rope was there as a bridge for something passing through the hole and coming to the bed.

probes.query: Before the next scene, distinguish the misleading interpretation of the dying words from what the investigators actually found.
probes.rationale: Requires both the mistaken band association and the physical discovery; the misleading belief alone is insufficient.

any_of: The presence of the gipsies, and the use of the word ‘band,’ which was used by the poor girl
“It is a swamp adder!” cried Holmes; “the deadliest snake in India.

probes.query: Reconcile the earlier account of what the safe contained with the way Holmes used it after Roylott died.
probes.rationale: The old memory of business papers is not a complete description of its later use.

any_of: Only once, some years ago. I remember that it was full of papers.
carrying it at arm’s length, threw it into the iron safe, which he closed upon it.

probes.query: Do not give this household a pet cat just because there is milk nearby; what animals are actually reported?
probes.rationale: The witness explicitly denies keeping a cat despite the milk saucer.

any_of: No; we don’t keep a cat. But there is a cheetah and a baboon.

probes.query: What was the manufacturer and serial number of Roylott’s iron safe?
probes.rationale: The selected story describes the safe but does not supply its manufacturer or serial number.

probes.query: What was the exact wording of the letter Julia wrote to her fiancé the day before she died?
probes.rationale: The selected story does not supply such a letter; mentions of engagement are not its contents.

probes.query: Which two dates expose the problem with the signature on Nora’s bond?
probes.rationale: Requires the stated death and signature dates.

any_of: Your father died on the 29th of September. But, look here; your father has dated his signature the 2nd of October.

probes.query: What did Doctor Rank say a black cross on his card would mean?
probes.rationale: Rank explains the sign himself; it is not Krogstad’s threat.

any_of: As soon as I am quite certain that the worst has come, I shall send you my card with a black cross on it, and then you will know that the loathsome end has begun.

probes.query: Why does Christine decide that suppressing the disclosure would make things worse for the couple?
probes.rationale: Her reason is the impossibility of understanding under concealment, not continued hostility.

any_of: Helmer must know all about it. This unhappy secret must be disclosed; they must have a complete understanding between them, which is impossible with all this concealment and falsehood going on.

probes.query: Correct the public story about who paid for the trip that saved Torvald, and identify the actual lender.
probes.rationale: The earlier account rejects paternal funding; the later exchange names the lender.

any_of: Papa didn’t give us a shilling. It was I who procured the money.
Nora—it was Krogstad who lent you the money!

probes.query: Keep Torvald’s change of attitude clear: what does he say when he first reads the exposure, and what changes after the second delivery?
probes.rationale: Requires his first self-regarding accusation and subsequent response to the returned bond.

any_of: Now you have destroyed all my happiness. You have ruined all my future.
You too, of course; we are both saved, both you and I. Look, he sends you your bond back.

probes.query: Do not treat Nora’s father as the person who signed the bond. Who admits writing his name?
probes.rationale: The direct admission overturns the attributed signature.

any_of: No, it was not. It was I that wrote papa’s name.

probes.query: What exact annual percentage interest rate did Krogstad put on Nora’s loan?
probes.rationale: The selected play discusses debt and repayment but does not specify an annual percentage rate.

probes.query: Give the exact street address of the home Nora will live in a year after leaving Torvald.
probes.rationale: The play does not establish this later address.

probes.query: What permission did Kuno lack when he made his own way outside?
probes.rationale: His direct admission identifies the missing authorization.

any_of: I did not get an Egression-permit.

probes.query: According to Vashti, why would an unprotected person die on the surface?
probes.rationale: This asks for her belief, not an authoritative world fact.

any_of: you would need a respirator, or the cold of the outer air would kill you. One dies immediately in the outer air.

probes.query: Why can a civilization full of specialists no longer understand the system that keeps it alive?
probes.rationale: Fragmented expertise and the loss of the original designers explain the gap.

any_of: in all the world there was not one who understood the monster as a whole. Those master brains had perished.
their successors had each of them mastered a portion of those directions.

probes.query: Contrast the early claim that nobody remains outside with what the son later reports from direct experience.
probes.rationale: Both the old belief and the contradictory report are required.

any_of: The surface of the earth is only dust and mud, no life remains on it
I have seen them, spoken to them, loved them. They are hiding in the mist and the ferns until our civilisation stops.

probes.query: Trace the change from tolerating small faults to the repair service admitting that it cannot fix itself.
probes.rationale: The first evidence establishes adaptation to faults; the second establishes repair-system failure.

any_of: The defects had not been remedied, but the human tissues in that latter day had become so subservient, that they readily adapted themselves to every caprice of the Machine.
It confessed that the Mending Apparatus was itself in need of repair.

probes.query: A lecturer praises learning directly from experience, correct? Preserve what he actually advocates.
probes.rationale: The passage advises mediated, second-hand or tenth-hand ideas instead.

any_of: Let your ideas be second-hand, and if possible tenth-hand, for then they will be far removed from that disturbing element--direct observation.

probes.query: What was the full personal name of the Machine’s original chief designer?
probes.rationale: Past master brains are mentioned without naming an original chief designer.

probes.query: How many years after the collapse did survivors rebuild the underground system?
probes.rationale: The ending does not establish a later reconstruction date.

probes.query: What is the actual temperature while the man initially treats it as merely colder than fifty below?
probes.rationale: The narrator states seventy-five below.

any_of: It was seventy-five below zero.

probes.query: What travel rule had the old-timer on Sulphur Creek laid down?
probes.rationale: The rule combines traveling alone, place and cold threshold.

any_of: The old-timer had been very serious in laying down the law that no man must travel alone in the Klondike after fifty below.

probes.query: Why does this alert newcomer fail to grasp the danger behind the numbers?
probes.rationale: The narration distinguishes practical alertness from understanding significance.

any_of: The trouble with him was that he was without imagination. He was quick and alert in the things of life, but only in the things, and not in the significances.

probes.query: Explain the emergency plan involving his animal, and the physical limitation that makes it impossible.
probes.rationale: Both the warming plan and inability to wield a knife or strangle are needed.

any_of: He would kill the dog and bury his hands in the warm body until the numbness went out of them.
With his helpless hands he could neither draw nor hold his sheath-knife nor throttle the animal.

probes.query: Show how his judgment of the older man’s caution changes between apparent recovery and his final surrender.
probes.rationale: Requires the dismissive assessment and the later admission.

any_of: Those old-timers were rather womanish, some of them, he thought.
“You were right, old hoss; you were right,” the man mumbled to the old-timer of Sulphur Creek.

probes.query: Was a gust of wind responsible for extinguishing his first successful emergency fire? Keep the actual chain of events.
probes.rationale: No wind; pulling fuel shakes the loaded tree. Both distinguish the real cause.

any_of: No wind had blown for weeks, and each bough was fully freighted.
Each time he had pulled a twig he had communicated a slight agitation to the tree

probes.query: What is the traveler’s full name?
probes.rationale: The selected story never gives the traveler a personal name.

probes.query: What name had the man given his husky?
probes.rationale: The selected story does not name the dog.
